quarterly_data.quarter: Digital Realty Bank of America conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management walked through why guidance moved from 8% growth (February) to double digits for this year and next. 'That resulted in a backlog at June 30 of $1.9 billion of signed but not commenced leases, including the lease we signed in July, post quarter end, that we reported on, which is a $400 million lease. We were at $2.3 billion. That $2.3 billion equals north of 30% of our in-place data center revenue.' The math he gave: 'As you look to that signed but not commenced revenue commencing, 31%, 32% on a base of $5 billion and change of data center revenue, you got more than 10% compounded.' He said Digital Realty will deliver double-digit growth this year, next year 'and potentially beyond that.'
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $1.9 billion at June 30 plus a $400 million July lease = $2.3 billion, north of 30% of in-place data center revenue on a base of $5 billion and change; more than 10% compounded

quarterly_data.quarter: Digital Realty Bank of America conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Development pipeline and the yield on it: 'We target 10%+ development yields,' and 'We have $20 billion under construction today, and 11.5% expected initial cash yield.' The pipeline doubled in six months - 'we have $20 billion of data center construction underway today versus $10 billion 6 months ago, or at the end of 2025' - even as permitting got harder. He stressed the yield is initial stabilized CASH on a fully loaded cost (land, generators, redundancy, contingency, losses to stabilization) and would be about 20% higher on a GAAP basis, 'so maybe your 11.5 would be 14.' Cost reference given for scale: 'a gigawatt of capacity could cost $15 billion.'
quarterly_data.figure: $20 billion under construction vs $10 billion 6 months ago; 11.5% expected initial cash yield vs a 10%+ target; a gigawatt could cost $15 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Digital Realty Bank of America conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The 0-1 MW / interconnection pillar hit a record in dollars, and AI is now visibly inside the enterprise business: 'We did $108 million of zero to one plus interconnection leasing this quarter. Not only was that a record, but we also had a record level of AI-related leasing or workloads embedded within that. It was north of 21%... Not only is the leasing up 28% year-over-year in the second quarter, but the percentage has also almost doubled.' Four of the last five quarters have been records, against $50 million a quarter two years ago.
quarterly_data.figure: $108 million of 0-1 MW plus interconnection leasing (record; up 28% year-over-year), AI-related north of 21%, versus $50 million a quarter two years ago

quarterly_data.quarter: Digital Realty Bank of America conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Re-leasing spread guidance raised: 'they were 25% in the quarter, which was almost anomalous type level relative to... the 7%, 8% guide we gave for the year at the outset of the year. Now we're expecting to do 10% for the year.' Split: 5.2% on the 0-1 MW side (historically a 2%-4% increaser, now 'above the high end of the range' on reduced availability) and 67% on greater-than-1 MW, 'driven by a handful of leases in APAC that were up for renewal.' He expects more quarters with meaningful upside volatility as fundamentals tighten.
quarterly_data.figure: re-leasing spreads 25% in the quarter; full-year expectation raised to 10% from a 7%-8% guide; 0-1 MW 5.2%; greater-than-1 MW 67% (APAC renewals)

quarterly_data.quarter: Digital Realty Bank of America conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Mark-to-market disclosure on the hyperscale book that the Q2 materials did not spell out: 'about 40% of our hyperscale rents are rolling between today and 2032... The expiring rates range from about $134 at the low end, up to as high as $160, but average really in that $140 range. We're signing new leases at $160 to $220 in that bucket. There's a meaningful upside opportunity between now and really the next five or six years.' The 0-1 MW book, roughly 40% of rent, stays a 2% to 5% per quarter increaser.
quarterly_data.figure: ~40% of hyperscale rents roll by 2032; expiring $134 to $160 (average ~$140) versus new signings at $160 to $220

quarterly_data.quarter: Digital Realty Bank of America conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Supply is running out in the core US market and permitting risk is now geographic. Northern Virginia: 'We are running out of available capacity in a place like Northern Virginia. We have 50 megawatts available today for lease, and probably another 96-megawatt building behind it. But after that, it could be some time.' Digital Realty is siting new capacity in markets like Kansas City instead. On moratoria: no new development exposure in places like New York or Pennsylvania; a temporary moratorium in Charlotte covers three projects that are all vested (two underway, the third buildable and approved). Customers are pulling delivery forward - asking for extra crews and paying for early handover ('May cost a little extra and they're paying for it') - because time to power is paramount.
quarterly_data.figure: Northern Virginia: 50 megawatts available for lease plus a 96-megawatt building behind it; three vested projects in Charlotte under a temporary moratorium
